description: One input switched or blended out to up to four outputs, in 2HP, driven by a knob, a voltage or a stream of triggers

params.text: Picks which output the input reaches, running from the first to the last of the ports in use across its travel
Attenuates and inverts the selection CV between -100% and +100%, and is ignored while the jack is in trigger mode
Turns on blending while it is green, so the signal crosses smoothly from one output to the next instead of jumping
Chooses how the jack beside it is read: green takes its voltage as the selection, red takes each trigger as a step to the next port
Limits the switch to the first two, three or four ports

inputs.text: Moves the selection, 10V covering the knob's full travel at full trim, or steps it on each trigger in trigger mode
A rising edge sends the selection back to the first port, and works only while the selection jack is in trigger mode
The signal being routed; an empty jack carries the voltage set on the menu, 0V unless you change it

outputs.text: Carries the input while this port is selected, or part of it during a blend, and 0V otherwise

notes: the selection jack and the reset jack read channel 1 only, so every channel of a polyphonic signal is switched together
menu: Trigger-order: Next, Prev, Ping-pong, Random, Random Diff — sets how each trigger moves the selection, and is used only while the CV jack is in trigger mode
CV normalized input — sets the voltage the signal input carries when its jack is empty
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Trigger-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming trigger counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-low detect-level — sets the voltage an incoming trigger must fall back below before the next one is counted, under 0.1V unless you change it

inputs.0:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
polyphonic

unpatched it reads a voltage set on the menu, 0V by default.
